title: Layouts
meta: Choose sidebar pages and a start page
intro: A layout is a named sidebar. Administrators choose its pages and optional start page, then make it a default for selected roles. Each person can choose another layout through their user menu.
A layout only hides pages. It never grants permission to open them. Docs remains available. Your role still controls access.
Use page selections that suit your staff. The pictures use a temporary Documentation review layout in a test installation. No sample data is required.
Edit general settings allows creating, editing and deleting layouts. View roles allows reading the role choices for defaults. Anyone signed in can choose an available layout.

tasks.title: Create a sidebar for a team
intro: Use this when a team needs a shorter sidebar and a suitable first page. Choose pages based on their work.
steps: Open your user menu at the bottom left, choose Settings, then select Layouts.
Open the page dots at the top right and select New layout.
Enter a clear Name. The example uses Documentation review.
Select the pages this sidebar should show. Choose at least one. Docs always remains available and is not a checkbox.
Open Start page and choose a selected page. The example chooses Reports. The default option is Dashboard.
Under Default for roles, select the roles that should use this layout by default. Leave them clear if people will choose it themselves.
Open the editor dots at the top right and select Save.
tasks.result: The table shows the saved layout, page count, start page and role defaults.

tasks.title: Change an existing layout
intro: Use this when a team needs a different set of pages. Users who selected the layout receive its saved changes.
steps: Find the layout and select its row dots.
Select or clear page checkboxes. The example adds Activity. Removing the selected start page clears that choice.
Open the editor dots and select Save.
tasks.result: The table reflects the saved page selection.

tasks.title: Choose a layout for yourself
intro: Use this when you prefer another available sidebar. Your personal choice overrides a role default.
steps: Select your user menu at the bottom left.
Open Layout. This menu appears when at least one named layout exists.
Select the layout you want. The example chooses Documentation review.
tasks.result: The sidebar changes to the layout pages that your role can open. Docs stays visible. A personal Start page choice can override the layout start page.

tasks.title: Return to the role default or full sidebar
intro: Use this when you want the administrator's role default again, or all pages your role permits.
steps: Open your user menu, then Layout. Select Role default to clear your personal layout choice. The menu names the current default in brackets.
To show every permitted page, open the same Layout menu and select Full sidebar.
tasks.result: The full sidebar returns. Permissions still decide which pages appear.

tasks.title: Remove an unused layout
intro: Use this when a named sidebar is no longer needed. Check the affected role defaults before deleting it.
steps: Open the correct layout's row dots and select Delete.
Check the layout name. People who chose it return to their role default. Roles using it lose that default. Select Delete layout to confirm.
tasks.result: The layout disappears from the list.

tasks.title: Edit layouts on a phone
intro: Use the same Layouts page on a phone. The Settings section list scrolls horizontally.
steps: Select Layouts in the Settings section list.
Open the layout row dots and choose Edit. Scroll the sheet to reach page and role choices.

end.title: Optional practice
paragraphs: In a test installation, create Documentation review with Dashboard, Reports and Forms. Choose Reports as its start page. Try it through the user menu, restore Full sidebar, then delete the test layout.

end.title: Limits
paragraphs: Layouts do not grant permissions or change the underlying data. Sidebar pages keep their standard order. Personal layout and start-page choices can override a role default.

end.title: Troubleshooting
paragraphs: A selected page does not appear. Check whether your role can open it. Adding a page to a layout does not grant access.
The expected first page does not open. Check your personal Start page choice in the user menu.
Role defaults cannot be read. The editor keeps existing defaults. Ask an administrator with View roles to review them.

end.title: Related guides
paragraphs: Read Roles for page permissions. Read User preferences for personal choices. Read Start here for command-line setup.
